subject: Running GLAD on three separate normalization runs?

messages.author: 8d5359408ef7b951
messages.subject: Running GLAD on three separate normalization runs?
parts:
Hi.

I'm trying to process multiple batches.
Two batches are tumor samples, one batch is normal samples (they are
not paired, but I have a large amount of normal samples).
I processed each using cRMA, where I used the following commands (on
each batch separately):

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("glioma,testSet",cdf=cdf)
print(cs)
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
print(acc)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
print(csC)
plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=
+300)
print(plm)
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
print(ces)
fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces)
print(fln)
cesN <- process(fln, verbose=verbose)
print(cesN)

I kept the data analysis of each batch (Normal, Tumor1, Tumor2) in
different directories, where the subdirectories of plm, acc and so on
were created in each directory separately.
Therefore my data structure looks like this
DATA/Normal/plmData
DATA/Tumor1/plmData

I now have separate cesN, and I would like to run GLAD, comparing the
two batches of tumor samples to the normal samples.
Each cesN object has a path, which I can see by doing getPath(cesN),
for example
getPath(cesN)
[1] "plmData/glioma,testSet,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/
GenomeWideSNP_6"

I think I need to change the path, so it includes the dir before I run
GLAD (so it will become "Normal/plmData/glioma,testSet,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,
+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6"). Is this correct?
If so, how do I do that? I tried searching for a command called
setPath(), but couldn't find it.

How should I merge the results from each separate normalization, so I
can run GLAD comparing the two tumor batches to normal files?

Thank you very much,

Uri David Akavia

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Running GLAD on three separate normalization runs?
parts:
Hi,

I've just got an offline reminder that this one wasn't answered yet.

On Wed, Jun 18, 2008 at 3:03 PM, Uri David Akavia
<uridavi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi.
>
> I'm trying to process multiple batches.
> Two batches are tumor samples, one batch is normal samples (they are
> not paired, but I have a large amount of normal samples).

One question is if you really want process them separately or
together. You are asking how to do it separately so I will answer
that below, but in case you want to combine two or more raw data sets
and then carry on with them as if they are one, you just do:

cs1 <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(dataSets[1], cdf=cdf);
cs2 <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(dataSets[2], cdf=cdf);
cs3 <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(dataSets[3], cdf=cdf);

cs <- clone(cs1);
append(cs, cs2);
append(cs, cs3);
rm(cs1, cs2, cs3); # Not needed anymore

When you then process the data, the full name of the output data set
will be the same as the fullname of 'cs', i.e. getFullName(cs). This
is the same as the name of the first data set you added, i.e.
getFullName(cs1). [In the next release of the package there will a
way to change the output name].

The rest of my reply will explain how to processes data sets
separately and then merge then at the very end.

> I processed each using cRMA, where I used the following commands (on
> each batch separately):
>
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("glioma,testSet",cdf=cdf)
> print(cs)
> acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
> print(acc)
> csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
> print(csC)
> plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=
> +300)
> print(plm)
> fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
> ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
> print(ces)
> fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces)
> print(fln)
> cesN <- process(fln, verbose=verbose)
> print(cesN)
>
> I kept the data analysis of each batch (Normal, Tumor1, Tumor2) in
> different directories, where the subdirectories of plm, acc and so on
> were created in each directory separately.
> Therefore my data structure looks like this
> DATA/Normal/plmData
> DATA/Tumor1/plmData

So, instead of using different working directories, in your case
DATA/Normal/ and DATA/Tumor/, I would recommend that you use the same
working directory for all your analysis. That should for most people
and that is how aroma.affymetrix is designed. If you do that, your
processed data will be outputted in the same probeData/, the same
plmData/ and so on. That is much more convinient.

>
> I now have separate cesN, and I would like to run GLAD, comparing the
> two batches of tumor samples to the normal samples.
> Each cesN object has a path, which I can see by doing getPath(cesN),
> for example
> getPath(cesN)
> [1] "plmData/glioma,testSet,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/
> GenomeWideSNP_6"
>
> I think I need to change the path, so it includes the dir before I run
> GLAD (so it will become "Normal/plmData/glioma,testSet,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,
> +300,A+B,FLN,-XY/GenomeWideSNP_6"). Is this correct?

> If so, how do I do that? I tried searching for a command called
> setPath(), but couldn't find it.

So, you don't want to do that, because that is against how
aroma.affymetrix is designed and supposed to be used; you should not
have to specify absolute paths, actually not even relative paths. If
your analysis scripts contain a path you are probably doing something
wrong.

It looks from you description that your two data sets have the same
names, that is, if you do getFullName(cs) in the two cases you get the
identical names: "glioma,testSet". You do not want to this, because
two data sets should not have the same full name if they are actually
different.

So, this is the setup I would suggest you to use. I'm not sure if the
tag 'testSet' is important to you or not, but I keep here as an
example:

rawData/
glioma1,testSet/
GenomeWideSNP_6/
*.CEL
glioma2,testSet/
GenomeWideSNP_6/
*.CEL
MyNormalDataSet/
GenomeWideSNP_6/
*.CEL

I strongly recommend, and ask you to please read the 'User Guide'
online [http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/users-guide],
and especially the first few section on the setup of directories etc.
Try to get a feel of the design of the package. If there is anything
unclear or ambiguous, please let us know how we can clarify it.

With the above rawData, you can process the two data sets like this:

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8, timestamp=TRUE);

# Setup the annotation data
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6", tags="Full");

dataSets <- c("glioma1,testSet", "glioma2,testSet", "MyNormalDataSet");
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(dataSets[1], cdf=cdf);
print(cs);

print(csC);

Repeating the above for all data sets separately would generate
normalized data sets:

probeData/
glioma1,testSet,ACC,,ra-XY/
glioma2,testSet,ACC,,ra-XY/
MyNormalDataSet,ACC,,ra-XY/

plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=+300);

print(ces);

Repeating the above for all data sets separately would generate chip
effect sets:

plmData/
glioma1,testSet,ACC,,ra-XY,AVG,+300,A+B/
glioma2,testSet,ACC,,ra-XY,AVG,+300,A+B/
MyNormalDataSet,ACC,,ra-XY,AVG,+300,A+B/

print(cesN);

Repeating the above for all data sets separately would generate
normalized chip effect sets:

plmData/
glioma1,testSet,ACC,,ra-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/
glioma2,testSet,ACC,,ra-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/
MyNormalDataSet,ACC,,ra-XY,AVG,+300,A+B,FLN,-XY/

If you do not want to process all your data again, you can rename all
dataset directories in probeData/, plmData/ etc accordingly and put
move the to the same place as above. That is safe to do.

>
> How should I merge the results from each separate normalization, so I
> can run GLAD comparing the two tumor batches to normal files?

It sounds like you can/want to treat the two tumor data sets
separately, and that you want to compare each tumor to the pool of the
normals, correct. Let's assume that your chip effects for the tumor
data set is 'cesN' and the chip effects for the normals is 'cesNRef'.
Then do:

# Calculate the average *file* of all fragment-length normalized chip
effects for the normals.
ceR <- getAverageFile(cesNRef, verbose=verbose);

# You then have to fake a reference *data set* containing this file replicate
cesR <- newInstance(cesN, rep(list(ceR), nbrOfArrays(cesN)));

# Setup the GLAD segmentation model
glad <- GladModel(cesN, cesR);

and process as "usual".

Hope this helps

Henrik
